strengths: The paper addresses an identifiable research audience in program analysis and code representation learning. Aligning LLVM IR with source code and generated comments is a useful direction, and the anchored encoders and staged interpolation form a coherent practical framework.

The reported results are promising across several tasks: POJ-104 MAP improves from CodeBERT’s 39.99 to 43.78, DIRE accuracy from RoBERTa’s 29.41 to 33.41, and summarization BLEU-4 from GraphCodeBERT’s 32.43 to 34.36.

The evaluation includes four task types, component ablations, a CodeT5 extension, and negative examples. Dataset counts, training settings, pseudocode, and an identified public code/data release provide useful foundations for reproducibility.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 evaluation protocol. Section 3.2 and Table 2 specify non-overlapping train/development/test problem labels, while Sections 2.3 and 4.2 describe supervised classification into 104 classes. A conventional classifier trained on 64 labels cannot substantiate the stated evaluation on unseen labels without an additional mechanism. If this is retrieval, specify the training objective, query/candidate sets, and exact MAP/MAR/MAF1 definitions. This ambiguity also affects the principal ablations.

Necessary: Clarify evaluation independence. Section 3.2 says summarization and reverse-engineering performance is evaluated on the validation set, whereas Section 4.3 describes test-set evaluation. Identify which split produced Tables 5–6 and how model selection was performed. Also document overlap checks across pretraining and downstream datasets, including duplicate functions and shared repositories; the manuscript does not establish contamination, but its current description is insufficient to assess this concern.

Necessary: Restrict the binary-analysis claims to the demonstrated setting or provide corresponding evidence. Inputs are compiler-generated LLVM IR, and Figures 7–8 retain informative function names and types; explicit function-name stripping is described for DIRE only. Source-generated IR and representations lifted from stripped executables are not trivially interchangeable, contrary to the introductory footnote. The present experiments support learning over the specified LLVM representation, rather than the full claimed scope of stripped-binary analysis.

Necessary: Separate interpolation benefits from training-budget and objective changes. PCL receives 10 epochs, whereas the full model receives 30 or 70; the secondary stage also introduces a different loss. Section 5.1 asserts convergence of PCL without presenting supporting evidence. A matched-budget comparison and a control using the secondary objective without learned interpolation would substantiate component-specific claims. Otherwise, conclusions should concern the combined training procedure rather than establish interpolation or gradual learning as the cause.

Necessary: Narrow or better substantiate the comment-quality conclusion. Table 7 reports MAP of 3.11 with human comments, 42.76 without comments, and 43.78 with generated comments. This striking collapse deserves investigation, but length distributions do not establish verbosity, implementation detail, or writing style as its causes. Document comment extraction, missing/repeated comments, alignment, and training stability. Without controlled comparisons, the supported finding concerns this particular raw-comment corpus and generation pipeline, not human versus synthetic comments generally.

Necessary: Calibrate semantic and statistical claims. Overlap metrics and selected examples do not establish executable correctness, semantic preservation, or long-term dependency handling. Summarization-reference provenance also needs explicit clarification, particularly given the CodeT5-generated comments. Functional checks or independent semantic assessment would support these claims; otherwise, restrict them to reference similarity. Likewise, single-seed results do not establish significant, consistent superiority: Table 6 shows lower BLEU-4 than GraphCodeBERT and only a 0.43 percentage-point exact-match advantage.

Necessary: Make the implemented method unambiguous. Figure 3 concatenates interpolation inputs, whereas Equations 8 and 10 sum them. Algorithm 1 permits mixing any two modalities, whereas Section 2.4 describes source/comment interpolation against binary embeddings. Clarify the actual sampling rule, interpolation-network dimensions, temperature, and gradient treatment of the trainable soft targets in Equation 5. Correct the Section 5.1 arithmetic: the MAF1 decreases are 0.79, 2.85, and 6.97 percentage points, not 2.07, 7.46, and 18.25 points.

Optional: Separate scalar and feature-wise interpolation ablations and quantitative embedding-neighborhood analysis would deepen understanding. Broader architecture comparisons would also be useful, but are not prerequisites for TMLR acceptance. The recommendation rests on unresolved evidential and communication issues, not insufficient novelty or impact.
